q: If 7x + 2 = 28, calculate the value of 7x − 1.
h: Don't solve for x. 7x + 2 = 28 means 7x = 26 — and the question only wants 7x minus 1.

q: Calculate the value of 2x² + 3y² − 4x + 2y − 17 when x = 3 and y = −2.
h: Substitute first, then do the exponents before the multiplying. y is negative, so y² comes out positive.

q: Calculate the value of (2 × 6³ + 6²) − 7 × 6².
h: 6³ = 216 and 6² = 36. Clear the parentheses first, then subtract 7 × 36.

q: Ellen's favorite lotion costs $3.00 for 4 fluid ounces. At that same rate, calculate what she would pay for a quart of lotion if a quart is equal to 32 fluid ounces.
h: Find the price per ounce and multiply by 32 — or notice that 32 is 8 × 4.

q: Determine at what point on a graph the lines y = 2x − 1 and y = 3x − 5 will cross.
h: They cross where the two y values are equal. Set 2x − 1 = 3x − 5, solve for x, then plug back in.

q: Nancy is knitting a baby blanket that requires 750 meters of yarn. There are 180 meters of yarn in each ball. Determine how many balls of yarn Nancy must buy to make sure she has enough yarn.
h: Divide 750 by 180, then round UP — you can't buy part of a ball.

q: Freddy reads 30 pages of his book on the first day. The next day he reads another 36 pages. On the third day, he reads another 42 pages. If he continues to increase the number of pages he reads each day by 6, how many days will it take him to read a book that has 270 pages?
h: The days go 30, 36, 42, 48… Keep a running total and stop when you pass 270.

q: State the term for an integer greater than 1 whose only positive factors are 1 and itself.
h: Its only factors are 1 and itself: 2, 3, 5, 7, 11…

q: If Kayla left a $10.47 tip on a dinner that cost $87.25, what percentage did she leave her waiter?
h: Part over whole: 10.47 ÷ 87.25, then move the decimal two places.

q: Calculate the common fraction that is halfway between the fractions 1/5 and 1/4, then reduce your answer.
h: Halfway between two numbers is their average. Give them a common denominator of 20 first.

q: A phone company charges $2 for the first five minutes of an international phone call and 30 cents per minute thereafter. If Malik makes a phone call that lasts 25 minutes, calculate the total cost of the phone call.
h: The $2 covers the first 5 minutes. That leaves 20 minutes at 30 cents each.

q: Brian paid his gym a one-time registration fee of $30 for boxing lessons. Additionally, he paid $20 per lesson. Determine the total amount he paid if he took seven lessons.
h: One flat fee plus a per-lesson cost: 30 + 20 × 7.

q: Calculate in hours and minutes the amount of time John worked if he started at 7:35 a.m. and worked until 1:20 p.m. on the same day.
h: Count up to noon first, then past it — the shift crosses 12:00.

q: Calculate the cost to fence the garden if fencing costs $0.35 per foot and the area of a square garden is 289 square feet.
h: A square's area is side × side, so the side is √289. You need the perimeter, not the area.

q: Jamie worked three hours on Monday, four hours on Tuesday, six hours on Thursday, and one hour on Friday; how many total minutes did Jamie work?
h: Add the hours first, then convert once at the end by multiplying by 60.

q: Tammy spent 55 minutes watching Stranger Things, 95 minutes watching Riverdale, and 35 minutes watching 13 Reasons Why; how many total minutes did Tammy spend watching Netflix?
h: Straight addition — the answer is already in minutes, so nothing to convert.

q: In a gaming club consisting of 80 members, one-fourth of them are boys. If no one leaves the club, what is the minimum number of boys that would need to join to make the club one-third boys?
h: A quarter of 80 is 20 boys. Set (20 + x)/(80 + x) = 1/3; the new boys grow both the top and the bottom.

q: Calculate, rounding to the nearest tenth, the volume of a cylindrical can which has a diameter of six centimeters and a height of six centimeters.
h: Volume = π × r² × h. The diameter is 6, so the radius is 3.

q: Determine the type of angle that ABC is if its measure is 67 degrees.
h: Under 90° is one thing, exactly 90° another, over 90° a third.

q: Calculate the number of possible combinations of who will serve as greeter during a four-night period if each night, either Amy or Matthew (but not both) serves as greeter at the door.
h: Two choices each night, four nights: 2 × 2 × 2 × 2.

q: Stacy has 6 identical black socks and 5 identical white socks in a drawer. If she selects without looking, determine how many socks she must take from the drawer to be sure of having a matching pair.
h: Worst case, she pulls one of each color first. What does the very next sock guarantee?

q: Explain how you could throw a ball as hard as you can and have it come back to you without it striking or bouncing off anything. There is nothing attached to it, and no one else catches it or throws it back to you.
a: Throw the ball straight up into the air.
o: Throw it into a strong headwind.
Throw it and run to catch it.
h: Gravity brings it back down. Which direction do you throw it?

q: A Petri dish hosts a healthy colony of bacteria. Once a minute, every bacterium divides into two. The colony was founded by a single cell at noon. At exactly 12:43 the Petri dish was half full. At what time will the dish be full?
h: It doubles every minute. If it's half full now, how long until it doubles once?

q: A study of 100 boys and 100 girls found that 60% of girls and 20% of boys enjoy the game Zombie Death. What percent of the children in the study who enjoy Zombie Death are girls?
h: 60 girls and 20 boys enjoy it — 80 kids in all. What fraction of 80 is 60?

q: Twenty people each competed in a scavenger hunt. Twenty percent of the people each found 80% of the items, and 80% of the people each found 20% of the items. Those who found the most items found a dozen items each. How many items were on the list?
h: The top group each found 80% of the list, and that came to 12 items. So 12 is 80% of what?

q: Jeff is younger than Rodney but older than Debbie. Larry is older than Erica who is older than Jeff. Rodney is older than Larry. Name the middle child in this grouping.
h: Line all five up youngest to oldest, then take the middle one.

q: Determine the probability that a person selected at random is less than 20 years old if, in a group of 120 people, 90 are more than 30 years old and all others are less than 20 years old.
h: 120 total, 90 are over 30, so the rest are under 20. Part over whole, then reduce.

q: There are 5 blue marbles, 4 red marbles, and 3 yellow marbles in a box. If Jim randomly selects a marble from the box, calculate the probability of selecting a red or yellow marble. State your answer as a fraction.
h: Red plus yellow over the total — and the total includes the blue ones.

q: Tommy randomly selects a card from a standard deck of 52 playing cards. Calculate the percent probability that his chosen card shows a red number greater than 6. Express your answer to the nearest hundredth.
h: Red cards only, and “number greater than 6” means 7, 8, 9, 10. Face cards and aces are not numbers.

q: At Andre's party, every person there shakes hands with each other once, and there are 45 handshakes. Calculate how many people are at Andre's party.
h: Each pair shakes once: n(n − 1) ÷ 2 = 45. Try small numbers until it fits.

q: A drawer contains five socks: two black and three blue. Determine the probability that two socks pulled out of the drawer at random will match. Express your answer as a common fraction.
h: Both black, or both blue. Count the ways for each, out of the 10 possible pairs.

q: If Sally has 3 pairs of pants and 4 shirts, and an outfit consists of 1 pair of pants and 1 shirt, how many distinct outfits can Sally make?
h: Every pair of pants goes with every shirt: 3 × 4.

q: A basket of fruit contains 5 oranges, 4 apples, and 6 bananas. If you choose a piece of fruit randomly from the basket, what is the probability that it will be a banana? State your answer as a common fraction.
h: Bananas over all the fruit — add all three kinds for the bottom.

q: In a box of 24 crayons, there are exactly four that are shades of blue. If Nick selects one crayon at random from the full box, what is the probability that he will select a crayon that is a shade of blue? State your answer as a common fraction.
h: Blue crayons over all the crayons, then reduce 4/24.

q: Calculate the number of distinct configurations that will result if Pedro has three cubes and he glues one face of each squarely to the face of another.
h: Face to face, the three cubes make a straight line or a bent one. That's it.

q: Determine which of the following figures would not be changed in orientation by a one-quarter (90 degree) rotation: a square; a regular hexagon; an equilateral triangle; a circle; a right trapezoid.
h: After a quarter turn, which of these looks exactly the same? One has infinite symmetry; one has four-fold.

q: Identify which of the following polyhedra (paw-lee-hee-druh) have the same number of faces: square pyramid; pentagonal pyramid; hexagonal prism; triangular pyramid; octagonal pyramid; rectangular prism
h: Count faces: a pyramid has its base plus one face per side. A prism has two bases plus the sides.

q: Determine which quadrant the line that passes through (0,4) and (1,3) will NOT go through?
h: The line drops one for every step right, so its slope is negative and it crosses at 4. Sketch it.

q: Calculate the amount of money in the account at the end of 6 months if a savings account earns 1 percent interest per month on the sum of the initial amount deposited plus any accumulated interest. The savings account was opened with an initial deposit of $1,000 and no other deposits or withdrawals were made.
h: One percent a month for six months is not six percent — the interest earns interest.

q: Which of the following pairs of angles are always congruent? A) supplementary B) vertical C) corresponding D) alternate exterior E) complementary
h: Which pair sits directly across from each other where two lines cross?

q: Calculate the sum of the 100 numbers in this series: 1 + - 2 + 3 + - 4 + 5 + - 6 + …+ 99 + - 100
h: Pair them up: 1 − 2 is −1, 3 − 4 is −1. How many pairs are there?

q: The lunch-ordering app for Savage Pizza asks you to choose two distinct meats from among pepperoni, Canadian bacon and sausage; or to choose two distinct vegetables from among mushrooms, onions, green peppers and black olives; or to choose one meat and one vegetable from among the same choices. Calculate how many different pizza combinations are possible using the lunch-ordering app.
h: Three separate cases: two meats, two vegetables, or one of each. Add them up.

q: On Saturday, three different baseball games are televised at noon and four different games are televised at 8 p.m. On Sunday, five different games are televised at noon. If Armando watches one Saturday game at noon and another at 8 p.m. and one game at noon on Sunday, calculate how many different combinations of games can he watch.
h: Multiply the choices: 3 times 4 times 5.

q: In a new Scrabble theme, a sequence of letters is considered a word if the first and last letters are consonants and every letter in between is a vowel. In this game, how many four-letter words can be formed using each of the letters D, R, A, G, O, N, T, U, and B no more than once?
h: First and last must be consonants, middle two vowels. Count the consonants and vowels available, then multiply.

q: Several students were trying out for a class play. When asked which roles they were willing to play, 12 of them were willing to play the knight, 15 were willing to play the troll, and 6 were willing to play the wizard. Of these students, 8 were willing to play either the knight or the troll, 5 were willing to play the knight or the wizard, and 4 were willing to play the troll or the wizard. Exactly 3 of these students were willing to play any of the roles. How many students were willing to play only the wizard and no other role?
h: Draw a three-circle Venn diagram and fill in the middle first.

q: In a race with five people, Alex finished ahead of Dustin, and the same number of people finished before Alex that finished after Dustin. Brandon finished before Casey and Alex finished after Peter. Who finished in third place?
h: Five racers, and the same number finished before Alex as after Dustin. That pins Alex and Dustin symmetrically.

q: At 10 a.m. a car dealer had 30 cars that were either blue or green. At 2 p.m. after selling 2 green cars and no blue cars, the dealer had 3 times as many green cars as blue cars. How many green cars did the dealer have at 10 a.m.?
h: After selling 2, greens equal three times blues, and the total is 28. Set it up as one equation.

q: While drawing with his computer tablet, Gabriel changed the dimensions of a rectangle so that the new rectangle was ½ as tall and ¼ as wide as the original rectangle. What is the ratio of the area of the new rectangle to the area of the original rectangle? Express your answer as a common fraction.
h: Half the height times a quarter the width. Multiply the two fractions.

q: A triangle has a base of 3 feet and a height of 6 feet. If its area is increased to 35 square feet by increasing the base and height by the same number of feet, what is the sum of the new base and height?
h: Old area is 9. New area is 35. Write (3+x)(6+x)/2 = 35 and solve for x, then add the new base and height.

q: Calculate how far Martin walked if he walked half of the total distance in the morning, stopping at noon for lunch. After lunch, he walked one-third of the remaining distance and still had 6 miles to go.
h: Work backwards. The 6 miles left is two-thirds of the afternoon half.

q: Calculate how many comic books Tim has if he has three times as many comic books as Betsy. Betsy has two-thirds as many comic books as Curt, and Curt has 27 comic books.
h: Curt has 27, Betsy has two-thirds of that, Tim has three times Betsy's.

q: What is the value of the expression 3x + 4y3 [3x plus 4y cubed] if x =3 and y= -2.
h: Substitute first: 3(3) + 4(−8). Watch the sign on the cube.

q: Shay is traveling at a rate of 75 miles per hour. How fast is Shay traveling in feet per second?
h: 75 miles is 396,000 feet; an hour is 3,600 seconds. Or remember that 60 mph is 88 ft/s.

q: How many ways can the letters in FACTOR be arranged so that the first and last letters are vowels?
h: FACTOR has two vowels, A and O. They must take the first and last spots — in either order.

q: Max worked five hours on Wednesday, two hours on Friday, and 55 minutes on Saturday. Gina worked four hours on Wednesday, 75 minutes on Friday, and two hours on Saturday. Who worked longer?
h: Convert everything to minutes before you compare.

q: Matt ordered three feet of yellow yarn, eight feet of green yarn, and nine feet of purple yarn. How many inches of yarn did Matt order?
h: Twenty feet of yarn altogether, and twelve inches per foot.

q: Christine ran 24 laps around her high school track. Each lap was .25 miles long. How many miles did Christine run?
h: A quarter mile per lap, 24 laps.

q: Calculate the average of the integers from 13 to 31, inclusive.
h: There are 19 integers from 13 to 31, and they're evenly spaced. The average is the middle one.

q: Calculate the probability that exactly two heads will be showing if three coins are simultaneously flipped. Express your answer as a fraction in simplest form.
h: Eight equally likely outcomes for three coins. Count the ones with exactly two heads.

q: Calculate the volume of a rectangular box in cubic centimeters if it measures 5 mm × 10 mm × 1 m.
h: Convert everything to centimeters first: 0.5 cm × 1 cm × 100 cm.

q: Calculate the percent probability that a randomly selected multiple of 3 less than or equal to 3000 is also a multiple of 5.
h: Multiples of 3 that are also multiples of 5 are multiples of 15. So one in every five.

q: Four friends are going to eat lunch at a table with 6 chairs. Calculate the number of seating arrangements for the four friends.
h: Four friends, six chairs, and it matters who sits where. That's 6 × 5 × 4 × 3.

q: Anna’s mother has four daughters. One is named April, one is named May, and one is named June. Determine the name of the fourth daughter.
h: Read the very first word of the question again.

q: Determine which word in the following list is least like the others: third, fourth, fifth, sixth, seventh, eighth, ninth.
o: Ninth is the only one over eight
Fifth is the only one with a v
Fourth is the only one that is a fraction
h: Say each one out loud and listen to the ending.

q: Complete the following syllogism – No reptiles have fur/All snakes are reptiles/Therefore….
h: If no reptile has fur, and every snake is a reptile, what follows?

q: Complete this syllogism – Either it is slimy or it is not green/It is not both slimy and green/Therefore…
o: it is both slimy and green
it is green but not slimy
h: Take the second statement first: it can't be both. So if it were slimy, it couldn't be green.

q: Calculate how many pieces that are exactly 5 inches long Sally can cut from a cord that is 7 feet long.
h: 7 feet is 84 inches. How many whole 5-inch pieces fit?

q: Calculate the number of chairs in a room if the room contains 23 rows of 27 chairs.
h: 23 times 27.

q: Four peaches cost a total of 90 cents. At this rate, calculate the cost of 3 dozen peaches.
h: Four peaches cost 90 cents, and 3 dozen is 36 peaches — that's nine groups of four.

q: Give the sum of the measures of all the interior angles in a rhombus
h: Four sides, like any quadrilateral: (n−2) × 180.

q: Give the sum of the measures of all the interior angles in a hexagon
h: Six sides: (n−2) × 180.

q: Give the sum of the measures of all the interior angles in an octagon
h: Eight sides: (n−2) × 180.

q: Give the sum of the measures of all the interior angles in a scalene triangle
h: Three sides — unequal sides change nothing.

q: Find the slope and y-intercept of the equation: 6x − 2y = 8
h: Rearrange each into y = mx + b. The number in front of x is the slope; the leftover is the intercept.

q: Find the slope and y-intercept of the equation: 7x = 10 − y
h: Rearrange each into y = mx + b. The number in front of x is the slope; the leftover is the intercept.

q: Find the slope and y-intercept of the equation: −6x + 3y = 15
h: Rearrange each into y = mx + b. The number in front of x is the slope; the leftover is the intercept.

q: Find the slope and y-intercept of the equation: y = 4x − 6
h: Rearrange each into y = mx + b. The number in front of x is the slope; the leftover is the intercept.

q: Calculate the number of diagonals that may be drawn in a hexagon
h: Diagonals in an n-sided figure: n(n−3)/2. Check that against a hexagon first.

q: Calculate the number of diagonals that may be drawn in an octagon
h: Diagonals in an n-sided figure: n(n−3)/2. Check that against a hexagon first.

q: Calculate the number of diagonals that may be drawn in a nonagon
h: Diagonals in an n-sided figure: n(n−3)/2. Check that against a hexagon first.

q: Calculate the number of diagonals that may be drawn in a decagon
h: Diagonals in an n-sided figure: n(n−3)/2. Check that against a hexagon first.

q: Calculate the number of diagonals that may be drawn in a dodecagon
h: Diagonals in an n-sided figure: n(n−3)/2. Check that against a hexagon first.

q: Determine the probability that a card selected at random from a deck of 52 cards is the suit of hearts
h: 52 cards, 13 hearts, 12 face cards, 4 tens, 26 black. Reduce each fraction.

q: Determine the probability that a card selected at random from a deck of 52 cards is a face card
h: 52 cards, 13 hearts, 12 face cards, 4 tens, 26 black. Reduce each fraction.

q: Determine the probability that a card selected at random from a deck of 52 cards is the number ten
h: 52 cards, 13 hearts, 12 face cards, 4 tens, 26 black. Reduce each fraction.

q: Determine the probability that a card selected at random from a deck of 52 cards is a suit of club or spade
h: 52 cards, 13 hearts, 12 face cards, 4 tens, 26 black. Reduce each fraction.

q: From a standard deck of 52 cards, give the probability of drawing a queen of hearts
h: Out of 52: one specific card, two black aces, four fours, two red sixes. Reduce.

q: From a standard deck of 52 cards, give the probability of drawing a black ace
h: Out of 52: one specific card, two black aces, four fours, two red sixes. Reduce.

q: From a standard deck of 52 cards, give the probability of drawing a number four
h: Out of 52: one specific card, two black aces, four fours, two red sixes. Reduce.

q: From a standard deck of 52 cards, give the probability of drawing a red six
h: Out of 52: one specific card, two black aces, four fours, two red sixes. Reduce.

q: Name the scientist who discovered that the ratio of the electromotive force to the current in a circuit is constant. This unit is named after him.
h: The unit of electrical resistance carries his name.

q: Newton's First Law of Motion states that objects in motion remain in motion unless acted upon by an outside force, and objects at rest stay at rest unless acted upon by an outside force. This statement is also referred to as the law of what?
h: An object's resistance to any change in its motion. One word.

q: Sara jumped off her rowboat into the lake. As she pushed her body forward, the boat moved backwards. Identify which of Newton's three laws best describes the motion of Sara and her boat.
o: the Law of Conservation of Mass
h: Every action has an equal and opposite reaction. Which law is that?

q: State the scientific term for the process in which a substance goes directly from a solid to a gaseous state.
h: Solid straight to gas, skipping liquid. The reverse of deposition.

q: Of silver, zinc, and iron, which would appear last on the Periodic Table with the highest atomic number?
o: they all have the same atomic number
h: Later on the table means a bigger atomic number. Which sits furthest along?

q: Of neon, nitrogen, and oxygen, which is the lightest and would appear first on the Periodic Table with the lowest atomic number?
o: they all have the same atomic number
h: Lightest means fewest protons. One of these has just 7.

q: Name the biological process where a single cell divides twice to produce four daughter cells.
h: Mitosis divides once into two. This one divides twice into four, and it makes sex cells.

q: Name the process by which living things with beneficial traits tend to survive and reproduce more than individuals with other, less successful traits.
h: Darwin's central idea — nature does the choosing, not people.

q: Name the type of symbiotic relationship that takes place when one member of the association benefits while the other is harmed.
h: One wins, one loses. Think of a tick on a dog.

q: Name the type of symbiotic relationship that takes place when both organisms benefit from the relationship.
h: Both win. Think of a bee and a flower.

q: Name the type of symbiotic relationship that takes place when one organism benefits while the other neither benefits nor is harmed.
h: One wins, the other doesn't care either way. Think of a barnacle on a whale.

q: Identify the type of land mammal, excluding humans, known to have the longest average lifespan at slightly over 60 years.
h: A land mammal, very large, famous for its memory.

q: Identify the serious respiratory illness that is highly contagious and can be fatal. The first case was reported in Vietnam in February 2003. It spread rapidly across Southeast Asia, as well as China, Canada, and the US.
h: A four-letter acronym. The first S stands for Severe.

q: Explain the cause of day and night on the earth.
a: rotation of the earth on its axis
o: the earth's revolution around the sun
the tilt of the earth's axis
the moon's orbit around the earth
h: The Earth spins once every 24 hours. What is spinning called?

q: Two objects on Earth are dropped from the top of a building that is 70 meters high. Object A has a mass of 12 g and object B has a mass of 6 kg. Assuming there is no air resistance, which object will hit the ground first?
a: Both objects hit the ground at the same time
o: Object B, because it is heavier
Object A, because it is lighter
Object B, because it has more momentum
h: Gravity pulls on both the same way. Mass is a red herring here.

q: The sedimentary rock shale becomes what metamorphic rock?
h: Squeeze mud-rock and it splits into flat sheets — good for roofs and chalkboards.

q: The sedimentary rock sandstone becomes what metamorphic rock?
h: Squeeze sand grains together hard and they fuse into a very hard rock.

q: Name the type of rock that makes up the ocean floor.
h: Dark, fine-grained volcanic rock — the same stuff Hawaii is made of.

q: Name the type of rock that includes limestone.
h: Limestone is made of shells and sediment pressed together.

q: Name the type of metamorphic rock that limestone becomes.
h: The stone Michelangelo carved.

q: Newton’s 1st Law of Motion is also known as the law of what?
h: An object keeps doing what it's doing. One word, starting with I.

q: Name the atmospheric layer that contains the ozone layer.
h: The layer that protects us from UV, sitting just above the one where weather happens.

q: In which layer of the atmosphere does weather occur?
h: The lowest layer — the one we live in.

q: Natural selection can also be referred to by what phrase?
h: Darwin's idea, in four words, coined by Herbert Spencer.

q: Give the term used in the field of genetics that refers to an organism’s appearance.
h: Pheno- means “showing.” It's the traits you can actually observe.

q: Name the phenomenon that is caused by the tilt of the Earth's rotational axis toward or away from the sun.
h: The Earth leans about 23.5 degrees, and that lean is why summer and winter happen.

q: Name the type of energy that results solely from motion.
h: Energy of motion. From the Greek for “to move.”

q: Give the classification that describes about 90 of the 118 elements on the Periodic Chart. They tend to be hard, shiny and have good electrical and thermal conductivity.
h: Most of the periodic table. Shiny, conduct heat and electricity.

q: Give the common classification that describes about a dozen elements on the Periodic Chart. They appear as metallic, but are brittle and have only fair electrical conductivity.
h: Between metals and nonmetals — the staircase elements like silicon.

q: Of metals, metalloids or nonmetals, which make up most living organisms?
h: Think about what living tissue is actually built from — the light elements, not the heavy ones.

q: Name the type of energy that is the sum of its kinetic and potential energy.
h: Kinetic plus potential. The word means “of machines.”

q: Waves of energy bend when they move around obstructions or pass through narrow openings. Name this type of bending.
h: Bending around an edge or through a slit. Starts with D.

q: Give the term that describes the very bright center of distant galaxies.
h: Extremely bright, extremely distant, powered by a black hole. Starts with Q.

q: Name the term for a sudden, intense brightening from a small area of the Sun's surface.
h: A sudden bright flash on the sun's surface.

q: Is this thousands, millions, billions, or trillions of miles from the Earth? the average distance to the Earth’s moon
h: The moon is about 240,000 miles away; the sun about 93 million. Mars is closer than the sun.

q: Is this thousands, millions, billions, or trillions of miles from the Earth? the average distance to the sun
h: The moon is about 240,000 miles away; the sun about 93 million. Mars is closer than the sun.

q: Is this thousands, millions, billions, or trillions of miles from the Earth? the average distance to Mars
h: The moon is about 240,000 miles away; the sun about 93 million. Mars is closer than the sun.

q: Define the term: carnivore
o: an animal that eats both plants and flesh
an animal that only eats plants
h: Carn is flesh, herb is plant, omni is all.

q: Define the term: herbivore
a: an animal that only eats plants
o: an animal that eats both plants and flesh
h: Carn is flesh, herb is plant, omni is all.

q: Define the term: omnivore
a: an animal that eats both plants and flesh
o: an animal that only eats plants
h: Carn is flesh, herb is plant, omni is all.

q: State the term for the offspring of a bird
h: It has just left the nest.

q: State the term for the offspring of a deer
h: Bambi.

q: State the term for the offspring of a seal
h: The same word as a young dog.

q: State the term for the offspring of a whale
h: The same word as a young cow.

q: State the term for the offspring of a rat
h: The same word as a young seal.

q: State the term for the offspring of a goat
h: The same word an adult might call a child.

q: State the term for the offspring of a kangaroo
h: It rides in the pouch.

q: State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in this neutral atom: silicon which has an atomic number of 14 and an atomic mass of 28
h: In a neutral atom, protons equal electrons and equal the atomic number. Neutrons are mass minus protons.

q: State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in this neutral atom: zinc which has 30 electrons and an atomic mass of 65
h: In a neutral atom, protons equal electrons and equal the atomic number. Neutrons are mass minus protons.

q: State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in this neutral atom: neon which is a Noble gas and has an atomic mass of 20
h: In a neutral atom, protons equal electrons and equal the atomic number. Neutrons are mass minus protons.

q: State the number of protons, neutrons and electrons in this neutral atom: oxygen which has an atomic number of 8 and an atomic mass of 17
h: In a neutral atom, protons equal electrons and equal the atomic number. Neutrons are mass minus protons.

q: State how many commas are needed in the following sentence, then identify where they should be placed: “They planned a route and they prepared their equipment.”
o: none; the sentence is already correct
h: Two independent clauses joined by “and” take a comma before the “and.”

q: List the three common types of figurative language.
h: Two of the three compare things — one directly, one using “like” or “as.” The third gives human traits to something that isn't human.

q: Written by Canadian author Margaret Atwood in 2019, The Testaments is the sequel to what dystopian novel originally published in 1985 that was later adapted into a popular Hulu television series?
h: Atwood's 1985 novel set in Gilead, later a Hulu series.

q: The following is what type of writing? “Should schools ban cell-phones?”
h: It's a “should” question with two sides you could take.

q: Change the following sentence from present tense to future tense: “The sisters are throwing a barbecue for the holiday weekend.”

The sisters are going to a barbecue for the holiday weekend.

q: Define the word “shatter” as used in the following sentence: “I saw the vase shatter when it fell from the shelf.”

a: above, higher, or more in quality or quantity
o: under, below, or lower in position or rank
fast, quick, or sudden in movement or speed
around, surrounding, or encircling on all sides

q: Restate the following sentence and include any missing punctuation. “Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee before school she went to Starbucks.”

o: Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee before school, she went to Starbucks.
Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee before school: she went to Starbucks.
Ms. Rodriguez decided to get coffee, before school she went to Starbucks.

q: Name the economic term that describes how much of a good or service a producer is willing and able to produce at different prices.
h: A market has two halves. The buyers' half is demand — what's the sellers' half called?

q: Name the economic term that describes property owned by individuals or companies, not by the government or by the people as a whole.
h: Not owned by the government, not owned by everybody. So owned by whom?

q: Name the economic term for a person, such as Bill Gates or Oprah Winfrey, who organizes, manages, and takes on the risks of a business.
h: What do you call someone who starts a business and carries the risk themselves?

q: Name the term that describes the government's constitutional power to take private property for public use as long as the owner is paid fair compensation.
h: They pay you fairly, but you can't say no. Two words; the second is “domain.”

q: Name the economic term that describes a situation in which unlimited wants exceed the limited resources available to fulfill those wants.
h: Wants are unlimited, resources are not. One word for that gap.

q: Name the economic term that describes an amount of money borrowed by someone that must be repaid, usually with interest.
h: Borrowed money you pay back with interest — the plain everyday word.

q: Identify the city and state where the Civil War started in 1861 when Confederate forces led by General Beauregard (bow-ree-gard) fired upon it.
h: Think Fort Sumter. Which South Carolina port is it in?

q: State the nickname used by Americans for the British soldiers stationed in America during the Revolutionary War.
h: It's about the color of their coats.

q: Identify the two countries where the US engaged in the “War on Terror” after the September 11, 2001, terrorist attacks.
h: One was invaded in 2001, the other in 2003.

q: Previously an actor portraying the president on a popular fictional Ukrainian television show, this man was actually elected President of Ukraine in April of 2019.
h: He played a fictional president on TV before the real job. Surname starts with Z.

q: On June 1, 2017, President Donald Trump withdrew the United States from this accord, focused on climate change mitigation.
h: Named for the city where it was signed, and it's about the climate.

q: On May 24, 2019, she announced her resignation as Prime Minister of the United Kingdom.
h: The UK's second woman Prime Minister, after Thatcher.

q: On December 6, 2017, President Donald Trump announced the recognition of this city as the capital of Israel, where the US embassy was eventually relocated months later.
h: Israel's government sits there, though most embassies were in Tel Aviv.

q: This acclaimed architect, who designed the Louvre Pyramid, died on May 16, 2019, at the age of 102.
h: Chinese-American architect known by two initials and a short surname.

q: Prior to his death on January 13, 2019, Alfred K. Newman was one of the last survivors of this group, whose indecipherable code contributed to the Allies' victory in World War II.
h: Their code was a Native American language the Axis never broke.

q: Following a referendum on June 23, 2016, this country voted to leave the European Union.
h: The vote was nicknamed Brexit. What does the B stand for?

q: Lasting from December 22, 2018 to January 25, 2019, this occurred and was the longest in U.S. government history.
h: 35 days over the winter holidays. What stops when Congress and the President can't agree on funding?

q: The Athenians led by Miltiades forced the Persians back to their ships in this 490 BCE victory, which legendarily inspired Pheidippides to run 26 miles with news of the battle.
h: A modern running race is named after the place this was fought.

q: Name the Roman emperor who ordered the death of his mother, may have kicked his wife to death, poisoned his stepbrother, and reputedly fiddled while Rome burned before he committed suicide.
h: He supposedly played music while the city burned.

q: In the third century BCE, Ptolemy I established a facility in which scholars copied, revised, and edited works of classical Greek writers. At its height it held about 500,000 papyrus scrolls before it was destroyed by fire. Give the location of this library in Egypt.
h: The great library sat in the Egyptian port city Alexander founded.

q: If you wanted to visit the world's oldest parliamentary institution, you would want to see the Althing, located 45 kilometers east of the capital Reykjavik in this European island country.
h: Its capital is Reykjavik.

q: State the first and last name of the president of South Africa who died in December of 2013 after a world-changing life.
h: He spent 27 years in prison before he became president.

q: Name the modern-day country where Ferdinand Magellan landed on 16 March 1521 thinking he had arrived in the Spice Islands. He would be killed by its natives a month later.
h: He died in the islands Spain later named for King Philip II.

q: This “window to the west” city lies on the Neva River near the Gulf of Finland. It was formerly known as Leningrad and contains the Winter Palace and the Hermitage Museum. Name this Russian city.
h: Named for a saint and a founding tsar. The Soviets called it Leningrad.

q: This philosopher's theory that the legislative, executive, and judicial branches of government should be separated inspired America's founding fathers. Name this French author of The Spirit of the Laws.
h: French, Enlightenment, wrote about separating the powers. Starts with M.

q: In April 1986, an explosion and fire at the Chernobyl nuclear power plant in the Soviet Union made it the site of the worst nuclear disaster in history. Name the modern-day country where you would find the 30-kilometer-wide “zone of alienation” today.
h: Chernobyl is about 60 miles north of Kyiv.

q: Identify the month that Congressional elections are held in even-numbered years on the first Tuesday after the first Monday.
h: Election Day is always in the fall.

q: List the three branches of the US government.
h: One writes the laws, one carries them out, one interprets them.

q: Identify the two US states that form the northern border of Florida.
h: The panhandle touches two states.

q: Identify the city and state where, on February 14, 2018, 17 high school students were killed in a mass shooting. Then name the person who has become an outspoken national leader of the #NeverAgain movement to “fight our nation’s gun violence epidemic.”
h: A high school in south Florida, February 2018. The student leader's surname is one syllable.

q: King Leonidas delayed a vastly larger Persian force under Xerxes I in a mountain pass whose name means “hot gates” at this 480 BCE battle.
h: Greek for “hot gates.” Three hundred Spartans held it.

q: Name the Roman emperor, successor to Trajan, known for his wall at the border between England and Scotland.
h: His wall still runs across northern England.

q: Name the war where Florence Nightingale focused on the sanitary design of hospitals and became known as “The Lady with the Lamp.”
h: Fought in the 1850s, largely on a peninsula in the Black Sea.

q: The Arkansas River begins in this mountainous state, where it flows through the steep Royal Gorge and past the city of Pueblo before entering the Great Plains. Name the state.
h: Its name is Spanish for “colored red,” which is also what the river is named for.

q: Name the North American mountain range that is named for the many waterfalls along the Columbia River Gorge.
h: Named for the falls. The range runs from northern California up through Oregon and Washington.

q: Name the 1954 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against segregating public schools.
a: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
o: Cumming v. Richmond County Board of Education
h: “Separate but equal” was struck down. The city is the capital of Kansas.

q: Name the 1966 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against Arizona policemen, who failed to read a suspect his rights.
h: You've heard the warning read on television. The state is Arizona.

q: Name the 1896 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against a New Orleans man seeking to integrate railway cars in Louisiana.
o: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
h: The case that made “separate but equal” legal in the first place.

q: Give the economic term that refers to a share of money earned by an investment or a business and then given to stockholders.
h: A share of the profits paid out to shareholders.

q: Name the term economists use to describe the highest-valued alternative that must be given up in order to engage in a given activity.
h: What you give up is the cost of the choice you made. Two words.

q: Give the business term that refers to a group of people who are allowed by law to run a company, college, or town as a single business.
h: A legal body treated as a single entity, separate from its owners.

q: Give the economic term that describes a factor that encourages or motivates a person to do or buy something.
h: A reward or a reason to act — the carrot, not the stick.

q: Give the economic term used to describe something acquired with the intention to make money with it in the future.
h: Money put in now to make more money later.

q: Name the only two United States capitals that rhyme.
h: Both end in the same two syllables. One is in Massachusetts, one in Texas.

q: As of the 2020 census, what US state had a population greater than the entire population of Canada?
h: About 39 million people at the 2020 census, more than all of Canada at the time.

q: Name the economic term that describes consumer desire and means to purchase goods and services at a given price.
h: The buyers' side of the market.

q: Name the economic term that describes a plan for spending and saving money used by individuals, businesses, or governments.
h: A plan for money coming in and going out.

q: Name the economic term used for a person who buys and/or uses goods and services.
h: The person at the end of the line who actually uses the product.

q: Name the 1954 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against a segregating governmental body in Topeka, Kansas.
a: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
o: Cumming v. Richmond County Board of Education
h: Topeka is the clue — the case is named for the school board there.

q: Name the 1963 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against the state of Florida, which argued that the state only needed to provide lawyers to defendants in death penalty cases.
o: Brown v. Board of Education of Topeka
h: The right to a lawyer, even if you can't pay. The defendant's surname starts with G.

q: Name the 1944 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against a Japanese man who claimed internment during World War II violated his 5th Amendment rights.
h: Japanese American internment during World War II. The name is Japanese.

q: Name the 1919 U.S. Supreme Court case where the majority ruled against a socialist pamphleteer exercising unpopular free speech rights during World War I.
h: “Clear and present danger” came from this case.

q: State the following about the United Nations: The primary objective
h: It was founded in 1945, right after a war, and its headquarters is on the East River.

q: State the following about the United Nations: The war after which the United Nations was founded
h: It was founded in 1945, right after a war, and its headquarters is on the East River.

q: State the following about the United Nations: The city where its headquarters is located
h: It was founded in 1945, right after a war, and its headquarters is on the East River.

q: State the term referring to the amount of space that matter occupies.
h: Not mass, not weight — the one about space.
w: Volume is space taken up. Don't confuse it with mass (how much matter) or weight (gravity's pull on that matter).

q: State the capital city of the US state of New Jersey.
h: It's on the Delaware River, and it isn't Newark.
w: Trenton sits on the Delaware River. New Jersey is one of the capitals judges reach for because it isn't the state's biggest city.

q: State the term used when all members of a species have died and cannot be recovered.
h: Gone everywhere and for good, not just gone from one area.
w: Extinction is permanent and global. Extirpated means gone from one area but alive elsewhere; endangered means still hanging on.

q: Solve for a, if a = 17 x 13.
h: 17 × 10, then 17 × 3, then add.
w: Break it up: 17 × 10 = 170, and 17 × 3 = 51. Add them: 221.

q: Convert one centimeter to millimeters.
h: Milli- is a thousandth; centi- is a hundredth.
w: Ten. Milli- means thousandth and centi- means hundredth, so there are ten millimeters in a centimeter.

q: Determine the number of ways the letters A through F can be arranged.
h: Six choices, then five, then four… multiply them all.
w: Six letters in six positions: 6 × 5 × 4 × 3 × 2 × 1 = 720. That's 6 factorial, written 6!.

q: State the term for the moon's phase when it appears completely round.
h: Earth sits in the middle, so the whole lit side faces us.
w: A full moon happens when Earth sits between the sun and the moon, so the lit face points at us.

q: Identify the letter that serves as the only vowel in the word “rhythm.”
h: There is no A, E, I, O or U anywhere in the word.
w: Y is doing the vowel's job here. It's the answer to a whole family of tip-off questions about words like rhythm, myth and gym.

q: Identify the Canadian province that is the largest in area.
h: Read it again — the question says province, not territory.
w: Quebec is the largest province. Nunavut is bigger but it is a territory — that word in the question is the trap.

q: State the US postal abbreviation for the state of Idaho.
h: Two letters, and Iowa already claimed IA.
w: ID. Watch the near-misses: IA is Iowa, IN is Indiana, IL is Illinois.

q: State the metric unit used to measure force.
h: Named for the man who wrote the three laws of motion.
w: The newton — the force that accelerates one kilogram at one meter per second squared. Named for Isaac Newton, so it's capitalized as a person but lowercase as a unit.

q: Solve for the number if you add two-fifths of a number to the number and got 56.
h: Call it n. Then n + ⅖n = 56.
w: Let n be the number: n + ⅖n = 56, so ⁷⁄₅n = 56, so n = 56 × ⁵⁄₇ = 40.

q: Identify the natural boundary which forms the border between the US and Mexico.
h: It's a river, and it runs along Texas.
w: The Rio Grande. It forms the entire Texas–Mexico border; the rest of the boundary is surveyed line, not river.

q: Calculate the arithmetic mean of the first five positive odd integers.
h: 1, 3, 5, 7, 9 — for evenly spaced numbers the mean is just the middle one.
w: The first five positive odd integers are 1, 3, 5, 7, 9. They sum to 25, and 25 ÷ 5 = 5. The mean of any evenly spaced list is its middle number.

q: State the name of the two governing bodies that comprise the US Congress.
h: Two chambers. The word for that is bicameral.
w: The Senate and the House of Representatives — together, Congress. Two chambers makes it bicameral.

q: State the term for underwater fissures from which magma erupts.
h: Volcanoes, but underneath the sea.
w: Submarine volcanoes. Most of Earth's volcanic activity happens underwater, along mid-ocean ridges.

q: State the possessive form of the pronoun “we.”
h: Two forms: one goes before a noun, one stands alone.
w: Our before a noun (our team), ours standing alone (that one is ours). Never write “our's.”

q: State the US postal abbreviation for the US state of Oregon.
h: Two letters, and it isn't OH.
w: OR. Not OH (Ohio) — the pair that catches people.

q: State the US postal abbreviation for the US state of New York.
h: Two letters: N, then the first letter of York.
w: NY. New Jersey is NJ, New Mexico is NM, Nevada is NV.

q: Calculate the area of a square with a side length of 22 units.
h: Side times side.
w: Area of a square is side × side: 22 × 22 = 484. Answer in square units, since area is always squared.

q: State the title of the Jack London book that tells the story of a dog named Buck.
h: London wrote two famous dog novels. This is the one where the dog goes TO the wild.
w: The Call of the Wild (1903), where Buck is stolen and taken to the Yukon. London's other famous dog novel is White Fang — that one runs the story in reverse.
